observation.visible_scene: Aerial close view of a powerful waterfall at the brink of a deep gorge. A dark, moss-topped rock outcrop sits at the edge in the lower-center/right of the frame, with muddy-white water spilling over the lip to its right and a vast, sunlit cloud of spray and mist billowing up from the plunge pool below, filling the left and center of the view. The falling water sheet is visible along the upper-right edge.
visible_changes: The camera slowly tilts and rotates, pointing more steeply down into the gorge: across the excerpt the rock outcrop drifts from the lower-center toward the bottom-right corner (and becomes partly cropped), while the cascading water on the right edge grows larger and occupies more of the frame.
The mist/spray cloud churns continuously and turbulently, its billowing texture and shape constantly reshaping and expanding upward, appearing denser and more filling as the view tilts down.
The water flowing over the right brink and around the rock outcrop moves steadily and continuously, with white froth surging past the rock's edges throughout.
The background cliff face on the upper-left shifts position slightly in frame, consistent with the camera's tilt/rotation rather than any motion of the rock itself.
outside_clip_unknowns: The full height and width of the waterfall and the contents of the plunge pool hidden beneath the mist are not visible.
What drives the water flow (river, rainfall) and the camera platform's full trajectory are unseen.
The scene continues beyond the last frame; no start or end of the flow or mist is shown.
uncertain_details: The exact camera motion (drone tilt/rotate vs. other) cannot be confirmed, only inferred from the consistent frame-wide shift of static rock features.
Whether the apparent growth of the mist is partly actual billowing or partly the result of the camera tilting into it is not fully separable.
The rock outcrop and waterfall edge are treated as fixed landscape features; their apparent movement is attributed to camera motion, not object motion.
